why: A colon SUBORDINATES the condition after it, where a full stop separates two independent thoughts. Admitting ':' to _CLAUSE_END reopens the meaning-inverting chop through different punctuation — which is exactly how the first fix for this failed. The quote INCLUDES the colon on purpose: that is the only shape the _CLAUSE_END exclusion actually guards. A quote stopping just BEFORE the colon is rejected by a different rule (only a full stop may be dropped from the end of a quote), so a case written that way passes whether or not ':' is excluded — which is how three unit tests came to look like they pinned this and did not. Verified by mutation: adding ';:' to _CLAUSE_END flips this case and leaves the naive shape green.
